slot.brief: P–V diagram of a cycle made of straight-line segments (e.g., rectangle or triangle); compute net work per cycle and state whether the cycle is clockwise or anticlockwise.

stem: A gas undergoes the cycle shown in the P–V diagram. Find the net work done by the gas per cycle and state whether the cycle is clockwise or anticlockwise.

verdicts.working: Net work is the signed area enclosed: the triangular area is ½(2 L)(3×10⁵ Pa) = 300 J, using 1 L = 10⁻³ m³. The path is anticlockwise, so work done by the gas is −300 J.

working:
$\Delta V=2\times10^{-3}$ m$^3$; $\Delta P=3\times10^5$ Pa; $|W|=\dfrac12\Delta P\Delta V=300$ J; anticlockwise $\Rightarrow W_{\text{by gas}}=-300$ J

Independent check: Net work is the signed area enclosed: the triangular area is ½(2 L)(3×10⁵ Pa) = 300 J, using 1 L = 10⁻³ m³. The path is anticlockwise, so work done by the gas is −300 J.
solution: The net work done by the gas is the signed area enclosed by the cycle. For the triangular loop, $|W|=\frac12\Delta P\Delta V=\frac12(3\times10^5)(2\times10^{-3})=300\,\text{J}$. The anticlockwise cycle gives $W_{\text{by gas}}=-300\,\text{J}$.

figure.description: Draw a P–V graph with volume V (L) on the horizontal axis and pressure P (10^5 Pa) on the vertical axis. Mark A at (1, 2), B at (3, 2), and C at (3, 5), with coordinates in the displayed axis units. Join A to B, B to C, and C to A by straight segments. Add direction arrows showing A → B → C → A. Label each vertex A, B, and C.
